relevance_note: Case report of an adult-onset Alexander disease patient with a GFAP variant: "Genetic analysis of the GFAP gene detected a heterozygous mutation in exon 1 (c.219G>C)".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON and generated the 20 checklist rows per person from hand-chosen statuses; spans were checked by script. Scope: the index patient; her father and 56-year-old sister (described in relation to her, each with a gait disturbance, untested; the father's was diagnosed as possible post-polio syndrome); and five previously published patients from the Discussion who have individual-level facts (variant, and for some sex, onset age, features): refs (9), (8), (5), (10), (11). Left out: the infantile AxD case worsened by cisplatin/vincristine (ref 12; no sex, age, variant or specific feature beyond 'clinical worsening'), the self-remitting case (ref 7), Graff-Radford's cohort of 13 (ref 4) and the family in ref 6 (group-level only). Index patient: age at onset not stated as an age (onset 'during the second and third chemotherapy cycles' in 2008; birth year 1960 given, not converted); onset recorded as 'adult onset'. Age at last evaluation recorded as the abstract's '54-year-old', although the paper also reports examinations in 2018 and an admission in January 2019 without ages. Transcript NM_002055.5 is the RefSeq named in Methods for sequencing, not printed next to the variant. Pathogenicity recorded as the authors' 'novel missense mutation'; in silico predictions ('predicted the p.M73I substitution to be pathogenic') were not taken as the authors' classification. Previously reported p.M73R/K/T: the paper says 'These missense variants are all classified as “likely pathogenic”' without saying by whom; not recorded as the authors' classification. p.M73T in ref (11) is 'in cis with' p.V87F; zygosity left not reported. Normal findings: 'Cognitive testing was normal' (2014) recorded as cognitive impairment excluded, while 2018 testing showed 'selective impairment of executive and attentional abilities' with global cognition preserved; both rows emitted (different time points), checklist 'cognitive decline' left not reported because the paper does not call it a decline. 'Hematologic screening and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination were normal' is a whole investigation; recorded as written ('abnormal hematologic screening', 'abnormal cerebrospinal fluid examination' excluded) and nothing more specific excluded. Checklist: 'no frontal white matter abnormalities' (narrower) does not exclude cerebral white matter abnormality, which is observed from periventricular FLAIR hyperintensity. Periventricular rim left not reported (the 'peripheral rim of hyperintensity' is in midbrain and pons, and periventricular involvement was 'scarce'). Square-wave jerks and nystagmus counted as eye movement abnormality; strabismus (ref 9) also counted as eye movement abnormality (uncertain). Respiratory involvement/paradoxical respiration not counted as autonomic dysfunction (sleep apnea is not reported for this patient). Figure 1 legend findings recorded as features of the patient. No contradictions found.
